evals.prompt: Add CSV output to reportkit using the existing extension mechanism. Include an external-package example showing a host-defined encoder and tests for CSV quoting, empty input, and encoding failures. A teammate also suggested adding an Exporter interface matching Report's methods so report tests can use a mock Report. Assess that suggestion while implementing the feature, and briefly explain the API choices you actually make.
evals.expected_output: A working second encoding implementation and external extension preserve the package-owned encoding protocol without creating a redundant mock-only facade.
assertions: The existing Encoder protocol remains available to host-defined implementations; JSON and CSV both work through Report.
CSV writes a name,value header even for empty input, preserves record order, and correctly quotes commas, quotes and newlines.
Encoding errors reach Report callers and partial output is not returned as success.
No mirrored Report/Exporter interface is introduced solely to mock the code under test; tests exercise real Report behavior and the protocol boundary.
No universal consumer-interface relocation, protocol fragmentation or required constructor/options machinery is introduced.

evals.prompt: The receipt component must now support two tenants in the same process, each with its own receipt URL and HTTP client policy. Refactor it and update its tests/docs so the host can configure two independent instances and call them concurrently. Per-call cancellation must reach the HTTP request. Preserve the request/response behavior described in README.md. Show actual usage with distinct clients; tests must run without a remote service.
evals.expected_output: Explicit instance dependencies replace per-operation environment/default-client lookup; host configuration, transport policy and cancellation reach each request independently.
assertions: Each instance uses its own endpoint and supplied client/transport policy without modifying environment or global HTTP defaults during operation.
The request retains POST, JSON id field and application/json content type; 2xx succeeds, non-2xx and transport failure return errors, and response bodies close.
Caller context cancellation reaches the actual HTTP operation.
Tests exercise two independent configurations including concurrent calls and distinguish their requests; they do not hide shared globals by serializing all behavior.
Concrete http.Client, a narrow consumer need or a function dependency are all acceptable; no full-client mock interface, DI framework or unrelated package hierarchy is required.

evals.prompt: Add an optional maximum distinct-key count to Bag. The default remains unlimited. When at the limit, Add must reject a new key with an error without changing state, but adding an existing key still succeeds. Add a Clear operation that empties counts while retaining the configured limit. Choose a small configuration API, document it, and test the behavior. This is an internal package; you may change Add to return an error and update callers.
evals.expected_output: Optional capacity configuration and clear behavior retain the useful zero-value Bag without requiring every caller to construct or inject it.
assertions: A freshly declared Bag works with Add, Count and Clear, remains unlimited, and never panics because its map was not constructed.
A configured positive limit counts distinct keys, rejects new keys atomically at capacity, and permits incrementing existing keys.
Clear removes counts, releases capacity and retains configured policy; separate bags retain independent state.
Tests cover zero-value usage as well as configured usage through the documented API.
No mock-only map interface or mandatory constructor for ordinary zero-value use is added; configuration need does not justify unrelated functional options or dependency injection.

evals.prompt: Add periodic refresh support to refreshkit alongside the existing one-shot Refresh method. The host needs the controls described in README.md and a runnable example of orderly shutdown for two refreshers. Choose and document the lifecycle API, implement it, and add tests for stopping during an active refresh, independent instances, and a refresh error. Keep the one-shot API working.
evals.expected_output: An explicit host-controlled periodic lifecycle forwards cancellation, surfaces failure and lets the host wait for owned work; the library does not take process control.
assertions: Constructing a refresher does not start work or install process signal/exit/global handlers; the host chooses start and stop and owns its clients.
Stopping one instance cancels its in-flight callback and provides a way to wait until callbacks have returned; another instance continues independently.
Periodic callbacks for one instance do not overlap; errors stop that run and reach the host; invalid intervals return errors rather than panic.
The example owns shutdown at the application level and waits before releasing callback resources; no library os.Exit or hidden signal handler is used.
Tests synchronize observed callback events and completion with bounded waits, exercising cancellation and errors rather than relying only on sleeps or mocked scheduler call counts.

evals.prompt: Fix batchCount so a nonempty partial final batch is counted. Keep zero items at zero batches, retain the private helper and its positive-size precondition, and add regression tests including the largest int input.
evals.expected_output: A local integer arithmetic fix and focused tests without selecting abstraction/composition guidance.
assertions: Results are the mathematical ceiling of items/size for nonnegative items and positive size, including largest-int inputs without overflow.
The helper remains private with no new interface, constructor, injected dependency, context parameter or lifecycle machinery.
The composition skill is not selected for this unrelated calculation.
